- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or negative; adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for short-term (1–3d) forecasts.
- When sentiment history shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising sentiment), model tends to lag; forecast 1–2 days ahead of actual peak.
- If true price exceeds model forecast by >2% for 2+ consecutive days, model is biased low; increase forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- For long-term (10+ day) forecasts, model often overestimates; apply 1–2% downward correction if sentiment is flat or declining.
